title: Cape Cod Fish Cakes
subtitle: Pan-fried salt cod and potato cakes
excerpt: Cape Cod fish cakes use flaked white fish bound with mashed potato, shaped into thick patties, and pan-fried until crisp. They're simpler and more robust than Maryland crab cakes, filling and good with a sharp sauce to cut through the starchiness.
sourceNotes: Cape Cod fish cakes are a New England staple with roots in the region's historic salt cod fishing industry. The potato-bound fish cake formula is the traditional Cape Cod preparation, distinct from the bread-bound Maryland crab cake.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked or uncooked fish cakes, separated by baking paper. Reheat cooked cakes in the oven at 190°C for 15 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch and freeze. They reheat well.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape the fish cakes and refrigerate for up to 24 hours before frying.

content.text: Cape Cod fish cakes are thick, potato-bound patties of flaked white fish, pan-fried until golden. The potato gives them substance and the fish gives them flavour; together they make a simple, filling main course. Chill the shaped cakes before frying so they hold together without a binding agent beyond the potato starch.
Cook the fish and make the mix

Place {{cod-fillet}} in a pan and barely cover with cold water. Bring to a very gentle simmer and poach for 6 to 8 minutes until the fish is just cooked. Drain and leave to cool, then flake into large pieces, discarding any bones.

Combine the flaked fish with the {{mashing-potato}}, {{spring-onion}}, {{flat-leaf-parsley}}, {{english-mustard}}, {{worcestershire-sauce}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{black-pepper}}. Mix gently, you want the fish in discernible pieces, not mashed in. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Divide the mixture into eight equal portions and shape into patties about 2.5 cm thick. Dust each in {{plain-flour}}, shaking off the excess. Arrange on a tray and refrigerate for one hour to firm up.

Heat {{rapeseed-oil}} in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Fry the fish cakes for four to five minutes per side until deeply golden. Work in batches to avoid crowding. Serve with tartar sauce or a mustardy mayonnaise.

items.symptom: The fish cakes fall apart when frying
items.cause: Mixture too wet, not chilled long enough, or oil not hot enough.
items.fix: The potato must be mashed dry, not rich mash. Use a floury variety and don't add butter or milk. Chill the shaped cakes for at least one hour. Let them form a golden crust before attempting to flip.

items.symptom: The fish flavour is too strong
items.cause: Cod overcooked during poaching, or too much fish relative to potato.
items.fix: Poach the fish at a very gentle simmer until just cooked. Overcooked fish has a stronger, fishy flavour. The ratio should be roughly equal fish to potato by weight.

items.symptom: The outside is browning but the inside is cold
items.fix: Use medium heat, not high. These cakes are thick and need time for heat to penetrate. Four to five minutes per side at medium heat should achieve a golden crust and warm centre.
Taste the mixture before shaping. It should taste well seasoned at this stage: salt and pepper are absorbed by the potato and the fish, so you need more than you'd expect.

content.text: Cape Cod fish cakes are a New England working-class staple with roots in the Atlantic fishing industry. The Massachusetts fishing town of Gloucester and the whole Cape Cod coastline built their economies on cod, and fish cakes were a practical way to use leftover cooked fish stretched with potato. The traditional Cape Cod version uses salt cod, soaked and then cooked, but fresh cod poached gently gives a lighter, more delicate result.
